# Incident Response: Evidence & Containment

Preserve evidence **before** containment actions that destroy it (deleting tasks, services or registry values).

## Suspicious Process Access to LSASS Memory

**Technique:** [T1003.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/) · **Rule:** [`T1003.001_lsass_memory_access`](../../detect/detections/T1003.001_lsass_memory_access/)

| Role | Action |
|---|---|
| SOC L2 | Pivot on the source process: parent tree, .dmp files written nearby (Sysmon 11), outbound transfers, and logons by accounts active on the host |
| Incident response | Treat as credential theft: isolate the host, reset every credential used on it since boot, hunt for reuse of those accounts |

### Evidence to collect
- ProcessAccess event with GrantedAccess and CallTrace
- Process tree of SourceImage
- Any dump file and its hash
- Logon sessions on the host since last reboot

### Containment
1. Isolate the host
2. Reset credentials of every account that logged on to the host since last reboot, including service accounts
3. Hunt for reuse of those credentials across the estate

## Suspicious Child Process of a WinRM Session Host

**Technique:** [T1021.006](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/006/) · **Rule:** [`T1021.006_wsmprovhost_suspicious_child`](../../detect/detections/T1021.006_wsmprovhost_suspicious_child/)

| Role | Action |
|---|---|
| SOC L2 | Rebuild the session from the target - 4624, WinRM 91 and every child of the same wsmprovhost.exe ProcessGuid |
| Incident response | Disable or reset the account used, isolate the source host if it is not an administration host, and hunt for the same account's WinRM logons elsewhere |

### Evidence to collect
- Process creation of the child, with its parent and command line
- Network logon (4624 type 3) and WinRM shell (91) on the target
- Every process started by the same wsmprovhost.exe

### Containment
1. Disable or reset the account used for the session
2. Isolate the source host if it is not an administration host
3. Block WinRM (TCP 5985/5986) from that source until reviewed

## Crontab Installed From Standard Input or a File

**Technique:** [T1053.003](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/003/) · **Rule:** [`T1053.003_crontab_noninteractive_install`](../../detect/detections/T1053.003_crontab_noninteractive_install/)

| Role | Action |
|---|---|
| SOC L2 | Trace the session that ran crontab (auth.log, parent chain) and review what the new job runs |
| Incident response | Remove the job after saving it as evidence, contain the account or service that installed it, and hunt for the same line on other hosts |

### Evidence to collect
- The cron table before and after the change
- Process creation of crontab with its parent chain
- Authentication records for the session (auth.log or journald)

### Containment
1. Save, then remove the malicious cron line
2. Lock or reset the account that installed it
3. Isolate the host if the job downloaded or ran a payload

## Scheduled Task Registered via PowerShell ScheduledTasks Cmdlets

**Technique:** [T1053.005](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/005/) · **Rule:** [`T1053.005_powershell_scheduled_task_creation`](../../detect/detections/T1053.005_powershell_scheduled_task_creation/)

| Role | Action |
|---|---|
| SOC L2 | Pull the registered task (4698 or Get-ScheduledTask), hash the action target, review 4104 script blocks and child processes |
| Incident response | Export then disable the task, quarantine the payload, isolate the host if the action already ran |

### Evidence to collect
- Command line
- Task definition from 4698 or Get-ScheduledTask
- Payload hash
- 4104 script blocks around the event

### Containment
1. Export the task definition
2. Disable and unregister the task
3. Isolate the host if the payload executed

## Scheduled Task Created With Suspicious Action

**Technique:** [T1053.005](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/005/) · **Rule:** [`T1053.005_schtasks_suspicious_creation`](../../detect/detections/T1053.005_schtasks_suspicious_creation/)

| Role | Action |
|---|---|
| SOC L2 | Pivot on the process tree, parent process, logon session and network activity; for /S, move to the source host |
| Incident response | Isolate the host if the payload executed; collect the task XML before deleting anything |

### Evidence to collect
- Process creation event and full command line
- Task XML (schtasks /query /xml or Security 4698)
- Parent process tree and user logon session
- Hash of the task payload
- Network connections from the payload process

### Containment
1. Preserve the task XML before deleting anything
2. Disable the task
3. Isolate the host if the payload executed
4. For remote creation, investigate the source host

## PowerShell Execution With Encoded Command

**Technique:** [T1059.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/) · **Rule:** [`T1059.001_powershell_encoded_command`](../../detect/detections/T1059.001_powershell_encoded_command/)

| Role | Action |
|---|---|
| SOC L2 | Review 4104 script blocks, child processes, network connections and DNS from the PowerShell process (±30 minutes) |
| Incident response | Block contacted infrastructure, remove persistence created by the script, isolate the host if a second stage ran |

### Evidence to collect
- Full command line and decoded script
- 4104 script blocks
- Parent process tree
- Network connections and DNS queries from the process

### Containment
1. Block the remote host or domain seen in the script
2. Isolate the host if a second stage executed
3. Remove any persistence created by the script

## Linux Shell Executing Decoded Base64 or Code From a Temporary Directory

**Technique:** [T1059.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/) · **Rule:** [`T1059.004_linux_suspicious_shell_execution`](../../detect/detections/T1059.004_linux_suspicious_shell_execution/)

| Role | Action |
|---|---|
| SOC L2 | Rebuild the process tree, review network connections and file writes of the tree, and check the account's recent sessions |
| Incident response | Contain the account or service that ran the code, isolate the host if a payload ran, and hunt for the same blob or file name on other hosts |

### Evidence to collect
- Process creation with the full command line and parent chain
- The decoded content or the file in the temporary directory, with its hash
- Network connections of the process tree

### Containment
1. Kill the process tree after saving its details
2. Lock the account or stop the service that started it
3. Isolate the host if a payload ran

## Rundll32 Proxy Execution From Suspicious Context

**Technique:** [T1218.011](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1218/011/) · **Rule:** [`T1218.011_rundll32_suspicious_execution`](../../detect/detections/T1218.011_rundll32_suspicious_execution/)

| Role | Action |
|---|---|
| SOC L2 | Review image loads (Sysmon 7), network connections and child processes of the rundll32 PID |
| Incident response | Quarantine the DLL, block contacted infrastructure, isolate the host if code executed; for comsvcs MiniDump follow the LSASS playbook |

### Evidence to collect
- Command line and referenced DLL
- Image loads (Sysmon EID 7) for the process
- Network connections from the process

### Containment
1. Quarantine the DLL
2. Isolate the host if code executed
3. Block any contacted infrastructure

## Run Key Persistence Pointing to Suspicious Location

**Technique:** [T1547.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/001/) · **Rule:** [`T1547.001_registry_run_key_persistence`](../../detect/detections/T1547.001_registry_run_key_persistence/)

| Role | Action |
|---|---|
| SOC L2 | Check whether the payload already ran (process creation at logon), its network activity and other persistence on the host |
| Incident response | Export the key, remove the value, quarantine the payload, isolate the host if it executed |

### Evidence to collect
- Registry event with full key and data
- Referenced binary and hash
- Process creation of the payload

### Containment
1. Export the key, then remove the value
2. Quarantine the payload
3. Isolate the host if the payload executed

## Kerberoasting - RC4 Service Ticket Requested for User Account

**Technique:** [T1558.003](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1558/003/) · **Rule:** [`T1558.003_kerberoasting_rc4_tgs`](../../detect/detections/T1558.003_kerberoasting_rc4_tgs/)

| Role | Action |
|---|---|
| SOC L2 | Count distinct SPNs requested by the client in the last hour, check LDAP SPN queries from the source, and logons from that host afterwards |
| Incident response | Rotate the targeted service account passwords, move them to gMSA or 25+ character passwords, disable RC4 where possible |

### Evidence to collect
- 4769 events for the client
- LDAP queries for servicePrincipalName from the source, if collected
- Logons from the source host afterwards

### Containment
1. Rotate passwords of targeted service accounts
2. Move service accounts to gMSA or 25+ character passwords
3. Disable RC4 where possible

## Suspicious Service Installation (PsExec-style / Command Services)

**Technique:** [T1569.002](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/) · **Rule:** [`T1569.002_suspicious_service_installation`](../../detect/detections/T1569.002_suspicious_service_installation/)

| Role | Action |
|---|---|
| SOC L2 | Find the network logon (4624 type 3) and share access (5140/5145) just before the 7045 to identify the source host |
| Incident response | Collect the service binary, delete the service, and investigate the source host as compromised |

### Evidence to collect
- 7045 event
- Preceding 4624 type 3 and 5140/5145 share access
- Service binary before it is deleted
- Source host of the network logon

### Containment
1. Collect the service binary
2. Delete the service
3. Treat the source host as compromised and investigate it

## Windows Event Log Clearing via Command Line

**Technique:** [T1685.005](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1685/005/) · **Rule:** [`T1685.005_event_log_clearing`](../../detect/detections/T1685.005_event_log_clearing/)

| Role | Action |
|---|---|
| SOC L2 | Recover the forwarded copy of the cleared log from the SIEM and review the hour before the clear; scope the account on other hosts |
| Incident response | Treat the host as compromised; preserve remaining logs and memory; reset the account if activity is unexplained |

### Evidence to collect
- Process creation event
- Forwarded copies of logs from before the clear
- User activity across other hosts

### Containment
1. Treat the host as compromised
2. Recover logs from the SIEM for the period before the clear
3. Scope the user account across the estate

## Password Spray - One Source Failing Authentication for Many Accounts

**Technique:** [T1110.003](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/003/) · **Rule:** [`T1110.003_password_spray_burst`](../../detect/correlations/T1110.003_password_spray_burst/)

| Role | Action |
|---|---|
| SOC L2 | Resolve the source to a host and process (who ran the binds or logons), check every sprayed account for a later success, and look for the same pattern from other sources |
| Incident response | Isolate the source host, reset the password of every sprayed account that later logged on, and review what those accounts accessed |

### Evidence to collect
- 4771, 4768 and 4625 events from the source for the window, with their failure codes
- Successful logons (4624, 4768) from the source after the burst
- Process and network telemetry on the source host for the window

### Containment
1. Block or isolate the source address
2. Reset passwords of sprayed accounts that logged on successfully, and revoke their sessions
3. Enforce smart lockout or a banned-password list for the targeted accounts

## Object ID Enumeration - One Client Walking Single-Owner Objects

**Technique:** [T1190](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/) · **Rule:** [`T1190_object_id_enumeration`](../../detect/correlations/T1190_object_id_enumeration/)

| Role | Action |
|---|---|
| SOC L2 | Confirm with the application owner which responses exposed another user's data and how many records were read |
| Incident response | Block the client, suspend the account used, fix the authorization check, and assess the exposed records for notification duties |

### Evidence to collect
- Access-log lines for the client and window
- Application records of object ownership for the IDs requested
- Authentication records of the account used

### Containment
1. Block or rate-limit the client address
2. Suspend the account used for the walk
3. Disable the vulnerable endpoint until the ownership check is fixed

## Kerberoasting - One Client Requesting Tickets for Many Service Accounts

**Technique:** [T1558.003](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1558/003/) · **Rule:** [`T1558.003_kerberoasting_volume`](../../detect/correlations/T1558.003_kerberoasting_volume/)

| Role | Action |
|---|---|
| SOC L2 | Resolve the source to a host and process, check for SPN enumeration (LDAP) from the source, and review logons with the targeted service accounts afterwards |
| Incident response | Rotate the passwords of every requested service account, move them to gMSA or 25+ character passwords, and investigate the source host |

### Evidence to collect
- 4769 events from the source for the window
- LDAP queries for servicePrincipalName from the source, if collected
- Logons with the targeted service accounts after the burst

### Containment
1. Rotate passwords of the requested service accounts
2. Move service accounts to gMSA or 25+ character passwords and disable RC4 where possible
3. Isolate the source host if the activity is not explained

## API Probing - One Client Rejected on Many Distinct Paths

**Technique:** [T1595.003](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1595/003/) · **Rule:** [`T1595.003_api_auth_probing`](../../detect/correlations/T1595.003_api_auth_probing/)

| Role | Action |
|---|---|
| SOC L2 | Review every request from the client for the window - successes, error pages, sensitive paths - and look for the same pattern from other clients |
| Incident response | Block the client at the WAF or proxy, review and fix any endpoint that answered 200 without valid credentials, and rotate tokens the client may have obtained |

### Evidence to collect
- Access-log lines for the client and window
- Any successful responses to the same client after the burst
- WAF or proxy records for the client

### Containment
1. Block or rate-limit the client address at the WAF or proxy
2. Disable any endpoint found serving data without authentication until it is fixed
3. Revoke sessions or tokens issued to the client
